text:
IncidentBot: [P1] Continuous-batching latency regression detected — high tail latencies in us-west-2 serving pool. Rule: cb_latency_p95 > 800ms for 5m.
Alex W: seeing alerts too. dashboards show p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.2s around 14:03 UTC.
Priya R: paging oncall, I'm on call for the next 40m. tagging @Josh M for runtime assist.
Josh M: I'm here, pulling traces. looks like queue depth spiked, microbatch sizes shot up to 32 on several hosts.
Ben T: any recent deploys?
Sasha K: no user-deployed model changes flagged. infra autoscaler did a small scale-in two minutes before the spike.
Alex W: interesting — scale-in may have reduced KV cache hits -> more cache misses -> longer token generation. can someone post the cache hit ratio?
eng-runtime-bot: kvcache_hit_rate avg=0.68 -> dropped to 0.22 at 14:03:12 for model-group:rlhf-13b; per-host variance high.
Josh M: that matches. continuous batch queueing increased because many requests couldn't use prefix KV cache; runtime fell back to full decode which increases microbatch time and pushes up queueing.
Priya R: customer impact? any 5xxs or errors?
Alex W: primarily latency. 5xx rate stayed flat. error budget not impacted but tail latency is affecting interactive customers. AcmeAnalytics and Fathom reported slower responses in support channel.
Ben T: can we throttle ingress or reduce max microbatch in prod quickly?
Josh M: we can push a hotfix via config change: set continuous_batch.microbatch_target=4 and continuous_batch.jitter_ms=8 and enable per_model_kv_prefetch=true for affected model-group. That should reduce per-microbatch wall time and smooth jitter.
Sasha K: apply at the routing layer? or runtime config?
Josh M: runtime config rollout — per-host update. I'll prepare a rolling change to avoid mass evictions. plan: update config on 10 hosts at a time with 30s wait and observe p95.
Priya R: do it. I'll coordinate customer comms. Alex, please craft a short note for support.
Alex W: posting to #support: "We observed elevated latency in us-west-2 due to KV cache pressure after autoscaler activity; mitigation in progress. No errors observed; will follow up."
Josh M: patch command (ssh-based one-liner for canary group):
```
for h in $(cat canary_hosts.txt); do 
  ssh $h 'sudo systemctl set-environment CONT_BATCH_MICRO=4 CONT_BATCH_JITTER=8 PREFETCH=1 && sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime' &
done
wait
```
Priya R: reminder — restart will clear warm KV cache for that host. do small canary and watch kvcache_hit_rate.
eng-runtime-bot: applied to canary hosts: 10/10. kvcache_hit_rate for canary avg=0.58 -> improved to 0.73 after 90s. p95 latency canary dropped 1.1s -> 240ms.
Josh M: encouraging. starting rolling update across remaining hosts in batches of 20 with 45s pause.
Ben T: any risk of causing bigger cache churn? restarts will clear local caches but lower microbatch target reduces per-request work so should net improve queueing.
Sasha K: metrics to watch: kvcache_hit_rate, cb_queue_depth, microbatch_size_hist, p95_latency, error_rate.
Priya R: I'll update the incident channel and ping ENG-SRE for visibility. please post update after the first two non-canary batches.
Alex W: support message updated: "Mitigation started: rolling runtime config change to reduce microbatch size and enable KV prefetch. We expect latency to improve within minutes; will notify when stable."
eng-runtime-bot: batch 1/5 applied. kvcache_hit_rate region overall increased 0.22 -> 0.46. p95 latency regional average 1.2s -> 620ms.
Josh M: batch 2/5 applied. kvcache_hit_rate -> 0.59. p95 -> 330ms. queue depth trending down.
Priya R: customers reporting improvements. Acme says interactive flows are back to normal. :thumbsup:
Sasha K: good sign. should we keep reduced microbatch target permanently? need perf/cost trade-off analysis.
Ben T: let's keep the config for the region for 2 hours then revert if no regressions. schedule a ticket for runtime team to propose more robust prefetch + cold-warm cache strategy.
Josh M: agreed. I'll hold the rolling update paused after batch 3 and monitor for 10m.
eng-runtime-bot: batch 3/5 applied. p95 280ms. kvcache_hit_rate 0.67.
Alex W: summary for post-incident: root cause likely autoscaler scale-in reduced warm cache population -> a cascade of cache misses at high concurrency increased microbatch durations -> queueing -> p95 cliff. Immediate mitigations: lower microbatch target + enable per-model KV prefetch rolled out.
Priya R: tagging @SRE oncall for postmortem ownership. creating incident ticket and will include timeline + command history.
Sasha K: notes for postmortem: include suggestions — avoid simultaneous scale-in + traffic spike, add soft-eviction policies, and implement in-memory shared cache across hosts for hot prefixes.
Ben T: also add automated gating: if kvcache_hit_rate drops >25% in 1m, pause scale-in.
Priya R: handoff to night oncall @Alex W in 20m. final status before handoff: p95 stabilized ~300ms, error rate normal, key customers confirmed improvements.
Alex W: I'll watch overnight. leaving runbook steps in the incident ticket and linking the exact commands used. thanks all. :clap:
